facts.statement: The only known species of Piveteausaurus is Piveteausaurus divesensis.
The partial braincase that serves as the type specimen for Piveteausaurus was first described in 1923 by the French paleontologist Jean Piveteau.
facts.quote: The partial braincase that became the type specimen of Piveteausaurus was first described in 1923 by French paleontologist Jean Piveteau

facts.statement: The type specimen was found by local collector Dutacq in the Marnes de Dives near Dives in Normandy, France.
facts.quote: MNHN 1920-7 was found by local collector Dutacq in rocks thought to be Oxfordian (Upper Jurassic), of the Marnes de Dives around the Vaches Noires cliffs near Dives in Normandy, France

facts.statement: The rocks containing the fossils were later reevaluated as being from the Upper Callovian stage of the Middle Jurassic, approximately 164 million years ago.
facts.quote: Later these rocks were reevaluated as older (Upper Callovian, Middle Jurassic, ~164 million years old)

facts.statement: The genus was established in 1977 by Philippe Taquet and Samuel Welles and named in honor of Jean Piveteau.
facts.quote: It was given its own genus in 1977 by Philippe Taquet and Samuel Welles: Piveteausaurus, named after Piveteau

facts.statement: Piveteausaurus is a theropod dinosaur known from a partial skull found in the Middle Jurassic Marnes de Dives of northern France.
facts.quote: Piveteausaurus (meaning "Jean Piveteau's lizard") is a genus of theropod dinosaur known from a partial skull discovered in the Middle Jurassic (164.7 to 161.2 million years ago) Marnes de Dives of Calvados, northern France

facts.statement: Piveteausaurus lived during the Callovian to Oxfordian stages, between 165.3 and 154.8 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Callovian to Oxfordian (165.3 to 154.8 million years ago)

facts.statement: Piveteausaurus is classified within the family Megalosauridae.
Piveteausaurus belongs to the subfamily Eustreptospondylinae.
A 2010 analysis by Benson found that Piveteausaurus most likely belonged to the family Megalosauridae, though its exact placement remained unresolved.
facts.quote: Benson in 2010. He found that while its exact placement was unresolved, it always grouped with a member of the clade Megalosauridae, and so most likely belonged to that family

facts.statement: The braincase of Piveteausaurus is comparable in size to that of a large Allosaurus.
facts.quote: The braincase is comparable in size to that of a large Allosaurus

facts.statement: In 2012, Thomas Holtz estimated that Piveteausaurus could have reached a length of 11 meters.
facts.quote: In 2012, Thomas Holtz gave a possible length of 11 m
